newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-WOOSNAM WINS BRITISH PGA BY TWO STROKES.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WOOSNAM WINS BRITISH PGA BY TWO STROKES.

text.p: Ian Woosnam of Britain overcame a faltering start before settling down on the back nine to win the British PGA title with a two-under-par final round of 70 on Monday.

The Welsh Ryder Cup veteran won by two strokes for his second victory in the championship after tasting success in 1988. He also took the World Matchplay title twice on the same course in 1987 and 1990.
"I didn't play my best golf today but I managed to get round. But the old heart was pumping a bit towards the end," he said.

South African Ernie Els and Nick Faldo of Britain both birdied the final hole for rounds of 70 to create a three-way tie for second with Irishman Darren Clarke, who could only par the long closing hole for a 71.
Woosnam, the 1991 U.S. Masters champion, finished on 275, 13 under par, to take the winner's cheque for 183,340 pounds ($300,000).
Els, Faldo and Clarke were on 277.
European number one Colin Montgomerie vaulted up to fifth place with an eight-under-par 64, the best of the week a day after he soared to a 76 in the third round.
Angel Cabrera of Argentina with a 69 and Englishman David Gilford after a 70 shared sixth place another shot behind.
